thread:
riley-sales: Hi all, CustY's vendor risk team sent back a SIG request (question-by-question). They want evidence for Q3, Q11, Q14, Q30 and a full answers spreadsheet. Timeline = EOD Thursday. Can ops/security help coordinate artifacts + upload method?

maria-sec: I can do control text review and map each SIG question to our standard control IDs. Don't include unredacted ARNs or secret dumps.

kai-eng: I'll extract config snippets and endpoint diagrams. Proposed file list: `Q3-auth-flow.pdf`, `Q11-data-flow.csv`, `Q14-kms-rotation.csv`, `Q30-pen-test-summary.pdf`, and `SIG-answers.xlsx`.

tony-ops: For residency scope (Q11) we should attach `region-policy.md` and `backup-locations.csv`. Note: prod storage in us-east-1, eu-central-1 for EU accounts.

legal-bot: Reminder: full pen test report requires active NDA. Exec summary OK to share now.

maria-sec: Good. I'll prepare short narrative answers for the SIG spreadsheet and remove "we plan" phrasing. Use conservative language: "We enforce", "We maintain", etc.

riley-sales: Upload method? CustY prefers their SFTP + checksums, but they accept presigned links if we also post a manifest. Which is easier?

kai-eng: We can do presigned links from `s3://sig-uploads/custy/` and include a manifest.txt with SHA256 lines. Example snippet: ```bash
sha256sum Q3-auth-flow.pdf > Q3-auth-flow.sha256
```

tony-ops: Ops prefers SFTP for audit trail. We have a dedicated account `custy-uploader@uploads.redwood.ai` and can chown files to an upload bucket. Both are doable but SFTP requires us to create the upload user and rotate credentials.

maria-sec: If SFTP, please ensure DLP scan runs on uploads and that we redact any secret-like strings before transfer.

legal-bot: CustY legal also asked for a signer name and title on the SIG spreadsheet (security contact). Who will be the signer?

maria-sec: I can be the security contact and sign the spreadsheet (Maria S., Head of Security Ops). I'll include a short attestation line.

riley-sales: Great. Any objections to zipping the package into `custy_SIG_package_2026-03-23.zip` and signing the manifest with GPG? They liked that in previous deals.

kai-eng: GPG-signing the manifest is straightforward. I'll generate `manifest.txt` containing file list + sha256 and produce `manifest.txt.asc`.

tony-ops: ETA for artifact collection + checksums is tomorrow noon. I can stand up the SFTP account by afternoon. Which do you prefer, Riley?

riley-sales: Go with SFTP if easy for ops. CustY legal prefers portal uploads but they agreed to SFTP this morning. Use the SFTP account and send credentials via 1Password shared note to the uploader.

maria-sec: I'll review the spreadsheet once Kai populates it. Also request adding `control-mapping.csv` that maps SIG question -> our control ID -> evidence file name. That accelerates their review.

kai-eng: Will add `control-mapping.csv` and a short README.md with instructions.

sec-bot: [automated] Checklist: redact secrets, include SHA256, include control mapping, ensure pen test NDA gating, add signer name.

riley-sales: Thanks team. Tony, Kai, Maria 1: please confirm when upload complete and I'll notify CustY.

kai-eng: Uploaded package to SFTP `sftp://uploads.redwood.ai/custy/` under user `custy-uploader`. Files: `custy_SIG_package_2026-03-23.zip`, `manifest.txt`, `manifest.txt.asc`, individual SHA256 files.

tony-ops: Confirmed DLP scan completed (no secrets found) and audit log attached: `upload-audit-2142623000.log`.

maria-sec: Final review complete. I signed the SIG spreadsheet and attestation. Sending signer details to Riley via DM.

riley-sales: Sent to CustY security team. They acknowledged receipt and asked for the pen test NDA path. I'll loop legal. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sec-bot: [automated] Thread will auto-close after 48h of inactivity.
